# Dick Moore

## Overview

- **Age:** Mid-30s (born approximately 12 years prior to his marriage at age 16-17; approximately 28 years before the events of Volume 5)  <sub>[v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021), [v2 c11 P28](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0028), [v4 c10 P46](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0046), [v4 c10 P49](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0049)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021)</sub>
- **Status:** Deceased  <sub>[v4 c31 P27](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0027), [v4 c32 P3](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0003)</sub>
- **Rank:** Sailor / Clerk  <sub>[v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021)</sub>
- **Origin:** Four Winds / Glen St. Mary, Prince Edward Island  <sub>[v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061)</sub>
- **Role:** Sailor and former store clerk  <sub>[v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021)</sub>

## Appearance

In his youth, Dick Moore was a handsome, big fellow with dashing ways, a high color, and a lean build, possessing a distinctive feature of having one blue eye and one hazel eye. After his departure on the Four Sisters, it was long believed that he had returned as a heavy, mentally impaired man with a thick beard. However, it was later revealed that the man who returned was actually his double and cousin, George Moore; the real Dick Moore had died years earlier in Cuba.

_Sources: [v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021), [v4 c9 P13](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0013), [v4 c11 P33](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0033), [v4 c13 P6](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0006), [v4 c31 P27](../source/v04-c31.md#nw-v04-c31-p0027), [v4 c32 P12](../source/v04-c32.md#nw-v04-c32-p0012)_

## Personality

In his youth, Dick was selfish, wild, and dissipated, possessing a small and ugly soul despite his attractive exterior. He was known to drink heavily, act carelessly, and pursue what he wanted relentlessly until he obtained it, only to lose interest afterward. He showed a tyrannical and domineering streak, leaving his young bride shortly after their forced marriage to go to sea.

_Sources: [v2 c11 P21](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0021), [v2 c11 P28](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0028), [v2 c11 P29](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0029), [v4 c8 P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 c11 P31](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0031)_

## History

Dick Moore grew up at Glen St. Mary as the son of storekeeper Abner Moore, working as a clerk in his father's shop in winter and going to sea in summer. Becoming infatuated with Leslie West, he pursued her despite her rejections, eventually forcing her into marriage at sixteen by threatening to foreclose the mortgage on her widowed mother's farm. Shortly after the marriage and the subsequent death of Leslie's mother, Dick left Four Winds on the ship Four Sisters bound for Cuba. For twelve years, the Four Winds community believed that Dick had been found in Havana by Captain Jim, suffering from brain trauma that left him a helpless, child-like invalid whom Leslie devotedly nursed. However, when Dr. Gilbert Blythe persuaded Leslie to send him to a Montreal hospital for an operation, the restored man was revealed to be Dick's cousin, George Moore. George disclosed that the real Dick Moore had actually contracted yellow fever and died in Cuba thirteen years prior to the surgery, before the Four Sisters ever sailed home.
